purpose.summary: UI states make interaction between the user and the application intuitive, efficient, and accessible by visually communicating the current condition of UI elements and giving feedback on user actions.
purpose.accessibility_requirement: Bosch UI element states comply with WCAG 2.1 accessibility requirements.

note.message: The content represents the standard definition for this topic. Depending on the digital touchpoint, such as Product UI, additional or deviating rules may apply.

categories.name: Interaction states
categories.definition: Interaction states help users understand which actions are possible and which action is currently being performed.
categories.purpose: They indicate availability and status of UI elements, communicate possible actions, and confirm user actions. Consistent use improves learnability and efficiency, reduces frustration, and increases user satisfaction.

groups.name: Conventional interaction states
groups.definition: Conventional interaction states characterize the visual and functional reaction of an element to user interactions such as hover, click, or unavailability, ensuring direct feedback and orientation.

states.name: Default
states.definition: The normal state of a UI element when there is no user interaction.
states.usage: Use this state to show that the element is available and ready for interaction.

states.name: Hovered
states.definition: Occurs when the user hovers the cursor over the element.
states.usage: Use to provide visual feedback, highlight interactivity, and signal that the user can interact with the element.

states.name: Pressed
states.definition: Activated when the user clicks or presses the element.
states.usage: Use to give immediate feedback that the user action has been registered.
states.trigger: Click, press, or active pointer interaction

states.name: Disabled
states.definition: Used when an element should temporarily not be interactable, for example because prerequisites have not yet been met.
states.usage: Use cautiously. Disabled states can reduce understanding, accessibility, and communication.
states.trigger: Element unavailable due to unmet conditions or temporary restriction

states.name: Focused
states.definition: Visual state that indicates which element, such as a button, link, or form field, has keyboard focus.
states.usage: Important for users who navigate with a keyboard instead of, or in addition to, a mouse or touchscreen.

states.name: Read only
states.definition: Applied to components when the user is allowed to review but not modify the component.

states.name: Dragging
states.definition: Occurs when a user presses and moves an element or component.

states.name: Typing
states.definition: Used when a user is entering or editing text.

categories.name: Selection states
categories.definition: Selection states specify the state of the selection of one or more elements by the user.
categories.purpose: They provide visual feedback on selected or available items, guide users through complex interactions, and help users keep track of decisions made.

recommended_use: Use this JSON as a compact knowledge representation for design linting, UX review prompts, component documentation, or design-token/state mapping.
Prefer interaction state definitions when assessing whether UI feedback communicates possible actions and current action status.
Prefer selection state definitions when assessing whether UI feedback communicates selected, deselected, mixed, active, or inactive conditions.
ai.state_category_decision_rule: If the state communicates what action is possible or being performed, classify it as an interaction state. If the state communicates selectedness or active membership in a set/navigation context, classify it as a selection state.
ai.disabled_state_decision_rule: Before using disabled, check if an active element with a hint, progressive disclosure, tooltip, or help text would communicate prerequisites more clearly and accessibly.
